newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ATHLETICS-TERGAT WINS BY THICKNESS OF VEST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-TERGAT WINS BY THICKNESS OF VEST.

text.p: World champion Paul Tergat of Kenya beat Ethiopia's Hapte Jifar by the thickness of a running vest in the season-opening IAAF World Cross Challenge on Sunday.
Tergat's margin of superiority was the smallest he had ever experienced in an international cross-country race.
Both runners were given the same time of 31 minutes 35 seconds but it was the Olympic 10,000m silver medallist who gained the verdict.
Jifar was clearly unhappy with the decision, claiming that Tergat had impeded him in the final few metres after the Kenyan had misjudged the position of the finish line.
Five seconds covered the first five, making the 10.5 km race one of the closest in the seven-year history of the series.
European champion Iulia Negura of Romania continued her good run of form by out-sprinting Ethiopia's Getenesh Urge in the six kilometres women's race.
Negura clocked 19:59 seconds, with Urge one second further back after Negura kicked for home 50 metres out.
Ethiopian runners filled four of the first six positions, with world champion Gete Wami third in 20:01.
Six women were in contention going into the last of the four laps but the race finished in a duel between Negura and Urge with half a kilometre remaining.
